titleTag: US Visa Wait Times: Mexico, Brazil and Colombia in 2026
h1: US Visa Appointment Wait Times in Latin America: Mexico, Brazil and Colombia
deck: Nogales was booking visitor interviews in about two weeks while Bogota sat past nine months. The region holds both ends of the global range, and the one country with a paid government fast lane is the one you probably cannot use it in.
metaDescription: US visa wait times across Latin America in 2026: every Mexican and Brazilian post plus Bogota, why the spread is so wide, and where the $750 expedite applies.

coverSpec.title: US visitor visa waits in Latin America ranged from about 15 days to about 270 in August 2026
coverSpec.desc: In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait ran from about 15 days at Nogales and Recife to about 270 days at Bogota, with Mexico City near 105 and Guadalajara near 180. Mexico is the only mission in the region participating in the $750 expedited appointment pilot. At several posts the interview waiver queue was far longer than the interview queue, reaching about 398 days at Bogota against 270 for an interview.
facts: Slower than interviews at many posts

faq.q: How long is the US visa wait in Mexico?
faq.a: It depends heavily on the post. In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait ranged from about 15 days at Nogales and about 45 at Tijuana and Matamoros, through about 90 to 105 days at Monterrey, Hermosillo, Merida and Mexico City, to about 180 days at Guadalajara. Student and petition-based categories were around 15 to 30 days at almost every Mexican post.

faq.q: How long is the US visa wait in Brazil?
faq.a: Short by global standards. In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 15 days at Recife, about 30 at Rio de Janeiro and Porto Alegre, about 60 at Sao Paulo and about 75 at Brasilia. Student and petition-based categories were around 15 to 30 days at every Brazilian post, and interview waiver processing was a day or two.

faq.q: Why is Bogota so much slower than the rest of the region?
faq.a: Bogota carries the whole of Colombia through a single consular section, while Mexico spreads its caseload across ten posts and Brazil across five. In August 2026 Bogota was around 270 days for visitor interviews against about 60 for students and about 15 for petition-based cases at the same post, which points to demand concentrated in the visitor category rather than a general capacity problem.

faq.q: Can I pay $750 for a faster interview in Latin America?
faq.a: Only in Mexico. Mission Mexico was the first mission designated for the State Department's expedited appointment pilot, and as of 19 August 2026 the only other one is Mission Canada. The fee is $750 per applicant, it covers B-1 and B-2 only, it is paid to the US government inside your own scheduling account, and the pilot is scheduled to close on 31 December 2026. No post in Brazil or Colombia participates.

faq.q: Is the interview waiver faster in Latin America?
faq.a: In Brazil, yes: waiver processing was a day or two at every Brazilian post in August 2026. In Mexico and Colombia it was often much slower than interviewing. Bogota showed about 398 days for a visitor visa waiver against about 270 for an interview, and several Mexican posts showed waiver waits of 200 to 330 days against interview waits of 15 to 180. Check both figures for your own post before choosing a route.

faq.q: Should I apply in Mexico if I live elsewhere in Latin America?
faq.a: No. Since the State Department's guidance of 6 September 2025, updated on 10 October 2025, applicants are directed to apply in their country of nationality or legal residence, and those who schedule elsewhere are warned they may find it harder to qualify. Fees are neither refunded nor transferred. Paying the Mexican expedite fee does not change where you are supposed to apply.

faq.q: Which Mexican post should I choose?
faq.a: Whichever your scheduling account offers with the shortest queue that you can realistically travel to, and check the current figures rather than the ones on this page. The spread across Mexican posts was about twelve to one in August 2026, which is the largest free improvement available to a Mexican applicant, but border posts and interior posts serve different populations and your account decides what you may select.

cta.heading: Most of this region does not need us, and Bogota might
cta.body: At 15 to 75 days there is very little a rescheduling service can improve, and we would rather say so than take a fee for it. Where the numbers do justify a conversation is Bogota near 270 days and Guadalajara near 180. If that is your post, tell us your current date and the widest range you could accept, and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth paying us at all.
